title: Today shows 1 of 4 pending items, not the money
observation: Home shows exactly four blocks: date, 'NEXT MOVE / Review a project decision / 2 decisions need your eye.', the editorial story, and 'ACTIVE ROOM'. My Studio hub (Profile → scroll) says '4 things need your eye': 2 overdue decisions, a $4,250.00 invoice due Sep 1, and an $18,500.00 proposal expiring Sep 8. Only the decisions surface on Today. The invoice and the proposal — the two items with real deadlines and real dollars — are invisible unless I go find Profile and scroll.
why_it_matters: My whole reason to open this app is to check on my house the way I check a package. If the one screen I land on shows a quarter of what needs my attention, I still have to go hunting for the rest every single day.
proposal_seed: Let Next Move's priority ladder surface a proposal-expiring or invoice-due branch, not just decisions and messages.

title: Active Room is a stranger's room, not mine
observation: The Active Room card reads 'Living Room / 2713 sq ft · 0 pieces saved.' I never scanned or typed that room. My real project — dining room + primary bedroom, per my own invoice's note — has no room representation anywhere. Signing out and back in (c-34) drops the card entirely, back to zero rooms.
why_it_matters: The one card that's supposed to be 'my house' on the home screen isn't. If I actually had a room in progress, I'd have no way to tell whether this card is mine or leftover from someone else's phone session.
proposal_seed: Scope local room storage to the signed-in user id, not the device, and clear it on sign-out/sign-in.

title: Story's 'new' dot never turns off
observation: The Maker Spotlight card 'The Grain Whisperer of Maine' carries a small clay dot in its corner every time I've looked at this screen across the walk — relaunch, keychain reset, dark mode, XXL — always present.
why_it_matters: A signal that's always on stops meaning anything within a week, and once I notice that, I stop trusting every other badge in the app too.
proposal_seed: Derive isUnread from a real last-viewed timestamp per user.

title: 'Today' never becomes 'good evening'
observation: The header always reads the literal word 'Today,' morning or night. I checked this at the default light-mode time and again in the dark-mode lane's identical layout — same word.
why_it_matters: I check this the way I check the weather — usually at night after the kids are down. A screen that can't tell 9pm from 9am doesn't feel like it's paying attention to my day.
proposal_seed: Read the existing TimeOfDay token on the home header, the way the Companion's conversation voice already does.

title: No search field anywhere in the app
observation: Looking for 'a sofa for our living room,' there is no search box on the Companion panel, the browse grid, or anywhere else — only filter chips (All/Seating/Tables/Lighting/Storage) applied after the fact.
why_it_matters: I don't browse for fun; I come in knowing what I need. Filtering 20 already-loaded pieces isn't the same as finding the one I want.
proposal_seed: Add a text search that queries the catalog, not just filters the current page.

title: Browse grid cards run off both screen edges
observation: The 2-column grid renders cards of at least four different sizes, the left column pushed partly off the left edge — one card reads only 'M & BOARD' with its price clipped mid-digit.
why_it_matters: This is the app's whole shop window. If I can't read a price or a name cleanly, I stop trusting anything else on the card, including the ones I can read.
proposal_seed: Fix the LazyVGrid item sizing constraint so both columns share one card size.

title: Every product page fails to load, no way out
observation: Tapping any card — saved or fresh — lands on 'Couldn't load product / Let's try that again.' Retrying repeats the same failure. There is no back button, no chevron, nothing else on screen.
why_it_matters: This is the one screen where I'd actually decide whether to trust a piece enough to ask Leah about it, and it never opens. I had to force-quit the app to get back to my own home screen.
proposal_seed: Qualify the vendors embed (vendors!products_vendor_id_fkey) in the product fetch — one-line fix, per ProductAPIClient.swift:99.

title: Dimensions and lead time never shown
observation: products.dimensions exists in the schema but is never returned by the recommendations RPC or decoded by the app; there is no lead-time or availability field anywhere the catalog reads.
why_it_matters: 'Will it fit' and 'how long will I wait' are the two things I'd actually ask before I let Leah spend $2,650 on a dining table. Neither can be answered from inside the app even when the page loads.
proposal_seed: Add dimensions to the get_recommendations RPC output and decode it in ProductModel.

title: A save today isn't remembered tomorrow
observation: The standard piece-detail entry never carries a room context, so 'Add to Room' always inserts a fresh, un-mirrored local row and 'isSaved' is never seeded from storage — the same piece shows 'Add to Room' again on a later visit and gets saved a second time.
why_it_matters: 'Save it, find it again tomorrow' is a named task for a reason — investment the app remembers is the whole return mechanic. Right now it doesn't remember, it just quietly duplicates.
proposal_seed: Seed isSaved from local storage on load and mirror every save to saved_items, not just room-scoped ones.

title: Saved opens on the empty tab
observation: 'Saved' opens on 'Boards,' which reads 'No boards yet' — the piece I actually saved lives one tap over, under 'All items,' a tab that doesn't default open.
why_it_matters: My first look at 'find it again' tells me nothing is there when something is. That's a wasted trip and a reason to stop trusting the count next to the Companion's Saved row.
proposal_seed: Default Saved to whichever tab actually has content.

title: A board can be created but never filled
observation: 'Create Board' works; nothing in the app ever calls addToBoard — every board stays 'This board is empty' forever.
why_it_matters: If I tried to make a 'Dining Room' board to gather ideas before I bring them to Leah, it would be a dead shell the moment I made it.
proposal_seed: Wire the card's Save/⋯ menu to call addToBoard with the active board id, or hide board creation until it does.

title: Saved can disappear from my only nav menu
observation: The Companion panel's 'Saved' row is present when I have 1 saved piece ('1 SAVED PIECE'), but the code gates it on a local room-items count, not the same count the row displays — a piece saved from Browse or the piece detail can leave the row absent entirely.
why_it_matters: The Companion is the only navigation this app has. A door that can silently stop existing means 'find it again tomorrow' sometimes has no path at all.
proposal_seed: Gate the Companion's Saved row on the same source of truth the row's own count reads.

title: My real rooms live nowhere I can check on them
observation: My invoice names 'Dining room + primary bedroom' as the scope; my decisions are about a rug and dining chairs. 'Your Spaces' shows exactly one room — 'Living Room,' 2713 sq ft, 'Manual Entry' — with no connection to either of my actual project rooms.
why_it_matters: 'See it in my room' assumes my room and my project are the same house. They're not connected at all — Your Spaces is a completely separate, empty concept from the dining room and bedroom Leah is actually furnishing.
proposal_seed: Surface the designer-defined project rooms (from proposals/invoices) inside Your Spaces, even without a client-side scan.

title: AR can never work — usdz_url is always null
observation: The room's 'IN AR' stat reads 0 in every shot I have; the RPC that feeds the catalog hard-codes usdz_url to NULL, so hasARModel is false on every code path — the AR button never draws and the Companion's 'Try in your room' says '3D model not available.'
why_it_matters: Seeing a $2,650 dining table in my actual dining room before I approve it is exactly the kind of thing that would make me trust the app with real money — it doesn't exist today, code-read, not device-tested by me. What would settle this: a device pass on a product row with a populated usdz_url.
proposal_seed: Populate usdz_url for at least a pilot subset of the catalog before promising AR anywhere in copy.

title: A color decision has no swatch
observation: 'Rug color — Natural vs Sand' presents two text-only cards, 'Natural' (Recommended, 'Warmer pairs with the brass') and 'Sand' ('More neutral - safer choice'), both $850, no image on either.
why_it_matters: This is a $850 color choice I'm asked to lock in from words alone. I'd text Leah for a photo before I'd tap 'Choose this,' which defeats the point of deciding in the app.
proposal_seed: Require at least one reference image per decision option before a designer can publish it.

title: No way to ask a question or defer on a decision
observation: The decision screen offers exactly two identical black 'Choose this' buttons. There's no 'ask my designer,' no 'not yet,' no way to say I need more information before an $850 choice ships.
why_it_matters: My tolerance drops the instant I have to leave the app to ask what a label means. This decision has no exit but a commitment.
proposal_seed: Add a lightweight 'Ask about this' action on the decision screen that opens a message to the designer, pre-filled with the decision context.

title: No way to compare two pieces side by side
observation: There's no compare surface anywhere — code-read confirmed (grep) and consistent with what the piece-detail screen shows when it loads at all: Share, Save, a maker-story card, no comparison of any kind.
why_it_matters: 'Is this the one' is a comparison question by nature. Without it, I'm holding two tabs in my head, or texting screenshots to myself.
proposal_seed: Let a save action target 'compare' as a lightweight two-up view, reusing the existing Saved data.

title: Buy it — the dead end, verbatim
observation: My actual dead end, verbatim, is 'Couldn't load product' / 'Let's try that again' — I never got further than the broken load screen. Companion (1 tap) → 'Your recommendations' (2) → tap any card (3) → the wall. Three taps to money, and the wall isn't a wall, it's a crash. Even reading the code for what the screen would show if it loaded, the terminus is still just 'Add to Room,' and once tapped, 'Saved ✓' — no cart, no checkout, no quote, no vendor link.
why_it_matters: If I wanted to buy a $200 side table myself, without looping Leah in, there is no verb in this app for that — buying happens by proxy, through a proposal she writes, or not at all.
proposal_seed: Fix the load trap first; then decide deliberately whether a small self-serve purchase path belongs here at all, given C24's finding that it would credit Leah nothing today.

title: Three different counts for one inbox, on one screen
observation: The Studio hub header reads '4 things need your eye,' the footer repeats '4 THINGS NEED YOUR EYE,' and directly below the header, 'Awaiting you' is labeled '3.' Home and the Companion both separately say '2 project decisions waiting.'
why_it_matters: I came here to get one clean number for what needs me. Instead there are three, on the same screen, and none of them agree.
proposal_seed: Compute one attention count from one source and reuse it everywhere it's displayed.

title: The whole Studio is behind an unlabeled avatar
observation: The only door to Studio — my projects, invoices, proposals, decisions, budget — is a 36pt monogram circle in the top-right corner of Home with no text label, reached via Profile → scroll.
why_it_matters: Everything I actually came to check on is two acts behind a tap that doesn't look like a menu — it looks like a settings avatar.
proposal_seed: Give the Studio a labeled, one-tap door from Home for any user carrying open items, not just a monogram.

title: 'Your studio' promises three things, delivers one
observation: The Companion's row reads 'Your studio / PROJECTS · MESSAGES · DECISIONS.' Tapping it lands directly on a bare projects list with a search bar — no messages, no decisions, no path to the real Studio hub (which lives only via Profile).
why_it_matters: The app's only nav surface just told me where I'd land and was wrong. That costs trust in every other row in that same menu.
proposal_seed: Point the Companion's 'Your studio' row at the actual Studio hub (StudioHubView), not the bare projects list.

title: The date you need is on the screen you leave
observation: 'Due Sep 1, 2026' appears on the invoices list, gone on the invoice detail. 'Expires Sep 8' appears on the proposals list, gone on the proposal detail. 'Overdue · Aug 22' appears on the Studio hub, gone on the decisions list.
why_it_matters: I check on my house to know 'when.' The one number I'm there for disappears exactly when I open the thing to act on it.
proposal_seed: Carry the same due/expires/overdue line onto the detail screen for invoices, proposals, and decisions.

title: 'Budget' is really one invoice's billing total
observation: 'Your budget / ACROSS YOUR PROJECTS' shows '$4,250 BILLED / $0 PAID / $4,250 OUTSTANDING' — my single open invoice — while my Projects list totals $725,000 across three projects. Only Aspen Loft Refresh appears; Birch Hollow and Marrow & Vale don't.
why_it_matters: 'Know where the money went' is my whole reason to open this. A screen labeled 'across your projects' that only counts one invoice on one of three projects tells me the wrong number with total confidence.
proposal_seed: Either rename this screen to what it is (invoice billing) or actually aggregate all projects' budgets.

title: A finished project sorts above active ones
observation: 'Birch Hollow / Completed / $185,000' sits above 'Aspen Loft Refresh / In Progress' and 'Marrow & Vale Residence / In Progress' in the Projects list. 'PHASE / Install' also truncates 'Installation & Styling' to a bare word.
why_it_matters: The project I'm mid-procurement on — the one I actually check daily — is buried under a job that's already done.
proposal_seed: Sort active/in-progress projects above completed ones by default.

title: No way to message my designer, anywhere
observation: 'Conversation 0 / No project conversations yet.' is the entire messaging surface — one line of grey text, no compose, no thread list, no 'message your designer' button.
why_it_matters: I have an overdue rug decision and an unpaid invoice on a $120,000 project. If I have a question, the app has no answer but 'text her outside the app' — which is exactly the email-thread loathing this app was supposed to replace.
proposal_seed: Wire the empty Conversation block to an actual compose action, even a simple message-to-designer form, before anything fancier.

title: 'Get design help' offered to a client with a designer
observation: The empty Notifications screen reads 'Updates from your designer will land here' directly above a 'Get design help' button — I already have Leah, and four things are waiting on me elsewhere in the app that this screen doesn't mention.
why_it_matters: This CTA is written for someone who's never engaged a designer. Seeing it as an existing activeProject client is a small but real 'this app doesn't know who I am' moment.
proposal_seed: Swap the empty-state CTA by tier — 'Message your designer' for activeProject/engaged, 'Get design help' only at discovering.

title: Nothing pushes for a proposal, invoice, or decision
observation: My Notifications feed reads 'Nothing yet' while four real items are pending across the Studio. Grounding confirms no backend trigger fires apns-send on a proposal, invoice, or decision anywhere in the codebase — only design-request and shipping-shaped events do.
why_it_matters: The app can only tell me something needs me if I happen to open it and look. That's not 'checking on my house like a package' — a package tells me when it moves.
proposal_seed: Add one invoke_edge_function('apns-send',…) call site on proposal-send and invoice-send — the pattern is already proven three times elsewhere.

title: A failed $4,250 payment gets one crowded red line
observation: Tapping 'Pay $4,250.00' produced 'Unable to start payment. Please try again.' inserted directly below the button, shoving 'Pay securely by card or bank transfer' half off-screen. The button keeps its full enabled look; there's no spinner and no distinct retry control besides tapping Pay again.
why_it_matters: The local 503 that triggered this is an environment fault, not a product one — but the UI it produced is real: a failed four-figure payment deserves more than a crowded caption and a button that still looks fine.
proposal_seed: Give a failed checkout hand-off its own error state: dim the Pay button, add a real retry action, keep the reassurance copy visible.

title: 'SIGNED' on a proposal nobody signed
observation: 'SIGNED (1)' headlines a $100,000.00 'Sample accepted proposal' whose real status is accepted, not signed — I have zero signed proposals in this account.
why_it_matters: I signed a real proposal back in June. If the app calls something 'signed' that isn't, I can't trust the word the next time it matters — including on my own history.
proposal_seed: Map the section header to the actual status enum — 'accepted' should read Accepted, not Signed.

title: The sheet I legally sign restates nothing
observation: 'Type your full name to e-sign. Signing confirms the scope and kicks off your project.' — that's the whole sheet: a name field and a button. No dollar amount, no date, no terms, no line items — while the terms one screen back read 'Deposits are non-refundable once procurement begins. Custom items are final sale.'
why_it_matters: I signed something like this in June without a second thought. Seeing it now, with clear eyes, it's not a document I'd want my name on without the numbers in front of me.
proposal_seed: Show the total and the binding-terms line directly on the sign sheet, not just the screen behind it.

title: Two weeks away looks exactly like two minutes away
observation: After a full force-quit and relaunch, my home screen is byte-identical to the one before I left — same Next Move, same story, same 'Living Room' card. Nothing marks the gap: no last-visit timestamp, no 'while you were away,' no unread marker anywhere on the screen.
why_it_matters: This is the whole test. Can I check on my house the way I check on a package? A package tells me it moved. This screen can't tell me anything moved, even when it did — I only find out by going and re-reading every Studio row myself.
proposal_seed: Add one honest 'since you were last here' line, computed from a real last-seen timestamp against Studio state deltas.

title: Nothing that matters to me can be shared
observation: The only Share buttons anywhere in the app are on catalog pieces. My rug decision, my $18,500 proposal, and my $4,250 invoice — the actual open items on my house — have no share control at all.
why_it_matters: If I want my husband's opinion on 'Natural vs Sand' before I tap 'Choose this,' there is no way to hand him the decision from inside the app — I'd screenshot it myself.
proposal_seed: Add a Share action on decisions at minimum — the highest-stakes, most time-sensitive screen a second household member would want to weigh in on.

title: The link I'd share opens the wrong app under the wrong name
observation: The one thing I can share — a piece — hands whoever I send it to a link titled 'Patina Designer Portal — app.patina.cloud.' The app has no associated-domains entitlement, so even if my husband has this app installed, that link opens Safari, not his copy of Patina.
why_it_matters: I'd be handing my own husband a link that says 'designer portal,' from an app I use as a homeowner, that can't even open his phone's copy of the app.
proposal_seed: Give the client-facing share URL its own client-portal route and title, and add associated domains so the link opens the app.

title: Dark mode: no Pay button in sight
observation: The dark-mode invoice detail, scrolled to the same 'No payments recorded yet' point that shows 'Pay $4,250.00' in light mode, has no visible Pay control at that stop — just the dimmed Companion orb and the footer.
why_it_matters: This is exactly when I'd be paying an invoice — after the kids are asleep, phone brightness down. If the button isn't where I expect it, I might assume the app is broken and text Leah to ask how else to pay.
proposal_seed: Verify the Pay button's dark-mode contrast/visibility at this exact scroll depth on device.

title: XL type: the Dynamic Island blots out my proposal's title
observation: At Dynamic Type XXL, the scrolled Studio list's top card — 'Aspen Loft — Living Room Refresh / Review by Sep 8' — is fully covered by a solid black status-bar pill drawn over the content, no safe-area inset reserved.
why_it_matters: I'm 47, and larger text is a real setting for me, not an edge case. At that size the one line I need — which proposal, and by when — is the line that's covered.
proposal_seed: Reserve a top safe-area inset on the scrolled Studio list so content never draws under the status bar/Dynamic Island.

title: Money rows are invisible to VoiceOver
observation: The Studio hub's Decisions, Invoice, Proposal, Invoices, and Budget rows draw chevrons and respond to taps, but an accessibility scan of the block at default text size returns none of them as buttons — only 'Open Living Room,' 'Retake Style Quiz,' 'Get design help,' 'Settings,' and Back.
why_it_matters: If I ever needed VoiceOver, the entire reason I open this app — checking my money and decisions — would be the one part of the screen I couldn't reach.
proposal_seed: Add explicit accessibility labels/traits to each Studio row so they register as buttons to VoiceOver.

title: Leah is named exactly once, nowhere to reach her
observation: 'Aspen Loft Refresh · from Leah Hartwell' on the invoice detail is the only place my designer's name appears anywhere in the app — no photo, no studio name, no bio, no contact button. Home, the project, the proposal, and the decisions never name her at all.
why_it_matters: Three months in, my designer is the whole reason I trust this process with real money. An app that shows her name once, in small type, on a bill, doesn't feel like it's on my side of the relationship — it makes me want to keep everything on text with her instead.
proposal_seed: Give the designer a persistent identity — name and avatar — on the project, proposal, and decision screens, not just the invoice.
